Greenlandic Name meaning: The Southern Glacier; sermeq meaning glacier, and kujalleq meaning southern
Fun Fact: Sermeq Kujalleq is the fastest flowing glacier in Greenland. It reached speeds of approximately 45 m/day in summer of 2012!

Greenlandic Name meaning: The Glacier of the Land toward the Fjord; kangia meaning fjord, nunaat meaning lands, and sermia meaning glacier
Fun Fact: Kangiata Nunaata Sermia is located at the end of Nuup Kangerlua, which is one of the longest fjords in Greenland and located next to Nuuk - the capital city!

Greenlandic Name meaning: Home of Hel in Old Norse, Hel was the Norse goddess of the underworld
Fun Fact: The calving front of Helheim Glacier has an ice cliff over 100 meters high! That is even taller than the Grimsby Dock Tower in NE Lincolnshire, UK!

Greenlandic Name meaning: The Great Gully Snowfield; sulussuaq translates to large gorge, and apusia means snowfield
Fun Fact: Between 2018 and 2021 Sulussuulip Apusiia North retreated more than 7 km, thinned by 20%, and accelerated by 300%!

Greenlandic Name meaning: The Rock Glacier; qarassaq translates to rock, and sermia means glacier
Fun Fact: Did you know, scientists drilled 1 km deep holes to investigate the subglacial drainage environment. You wouldn't want to fall in that hole!

Greenlandic Name meaning: Named after the German cartographer August Petermann during the European Arctic exploration in the 19th Century
Fun Fact: Petermann Glacier is one of the very few glaciers in Greenland that form a floating ice shelf, making it similar to glaciers in Antarctica!

Greenlandic Name meaning: Seventy-Nine Glacier, because it terminartes at 79ºN latitude
Fun Fact: Nioghalvfjerdsbræ forms part of the Northeast Greenland Ice Stream which drains 17% of the entire Greenland Ice Sheet! This is a very important glacier to understand.
Køge Bugt is the 4th biggest contributor to ice loss from the Greenland Ice Sheet since 1972, but it’s still surprisingly under-studied. Punching above its weight!

Greenlandic Name meaning: The Sheep Glacier; ulli translates to sheep and sermia means glacier"
Fun Fact: Harald Moltke Bræ is the only glacier draining the Greenland Ice Sheet that has surged this century. Most surging glaciers are found in Svalbard - is this glacier lost?

Greenlandic Name meaning: The Dark Soot Glacier; usuk/usulluq translates to soot
Fun Fact: Polonia Glacier terminates on land which means almost all of its mass loss is due to surface melting and runoff. No calving here!

Greenlandic Name meaning: The Big Fjord; kangerluk meaning fjord, and -ssuaq meaning big
Fun Fact: Kangerlussuaq Glacier is actually on Greenland’s east coast, even though it shares its name with a town and airport on the west coast. Don't get lost!

Greenlandic Name meaning: The Glacier of the Very Large Island; where qeqertaarsuk means very large island
Fun Fact: Tracy Glacier sits right next to Heilprin Glacier in northwest Greenland, but it is melting much faster because warm ocean water flows against its front while much colder water flows against Heilprin. Tracy is HOT, Heilprin is NOT!

Greenlandic Name meaning: The Glacier of the Place with Reindeer; tuttu meaning reindeer, -lik meaning to have, and -assaq meaning abundance
Fun Fact: Hayes Glacier experienced rerouting of the areas of fast flow linked to reconfiguration of hydrological network at the bed!

Greenlandic Name meaning: The Sunny Glacier; saqqaq meaning the sunny side and exposed face
Fun Fact: Saqqarliup Sermia dams a lake that drains every 5-10 years!

Greenlandic Name meaning: The Headland Glacier; isungu meaning headland and sermia meaning glacier
Fun Fact: The glaciers in this area of Greenland are some of the most studied thanks to the major airport nearby!

Greenlandic Name meaning: The Sand Glacier; sioqqaq meaning sand and sermia meaning glacier
Fun Fact: Sioqqap Sermia transports huge amounts of sediment, creating an outwash plain that has actually expanded the land area of Greenland!

Greenlandic Name meaning: The Middle Passage Glacier; akulleq meaning middle, and -arut meaning passage
Fun Fact: The surrounding area of Akuliarutsip Sermia have been studied by Finnish-Swedish geoloigst Nordenskiöld, contributing to the first description of cryoconite, a dark, biologically-active sediment that enhances glacier melt
